sources.entry: Bludit ⚠ - Build a site or blog in seconds. Bludit uses flat-files (text files in JSON format) to store posts and pages. (Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Bludit is a flat-file content management system written in PHP that stores posts and pages as JSON files, so it needs no database.
summary.what_it_does: Bludit is a PHP-based CMS for building websites and blogs. It stores content as JSON files instead of in a database. The README says it supports both Markdown and HTML for writing content. Installation is done by uploading the files to a PHP-capable web server and running the web-based installer. The README also mentions a Docker image (bludit/docker) and the PHP built-in web server for quick local testing. It lists plugins and themes as extension points, and an admin area for managing settings. A note in the README covers configuring the web server to pass real client IPs when Bludit sits behind a reverse proxy, which matters for its login brute-force blocklist and visitor statistics.
use_cases: host a flat-file website on shared PHP hosting
write posts in Markdown or HTML
quick local website testing with Docker
how_to_run: Download the latest version from the official Bludit site
Extract the zip file into a directory such as bludit
Upload the bludit directory to your web server or hosting
Visit your domain and follow the Bludit Installer
For quick testing: docker pull bludit/docker:latest
stack: PHP mbstring, gd, dom and json modules
notable: Flat-file design: content stored as JSON, no database setup required
Supports both Markdown and HTML content
Docker image available for quick testing
caveats: Requires a web server with PHP 8.0 or higher and several PHP extensions
Behind a reverse proxy, the web server must be configured to set the real client IP, or the login blocklist and visitor stats will be wrong
Upgrades require manual file replacement and cache purging, with a full backup recommended
